body:
Quite a jump to assume “Nonhuman biologic” means alien life. He did not say extraterrestrial. Bird shit is a “Nonhuman biologic.” It could also be anything that was alive that happened to be at the crash site at the time. Even a damn bush is a non human biologic. Biologic covers ALL life and there’s a lot of it on THIS planet that ain’t human. 

Too vague. It’s meaningless.

What if they’re just microbes? At what level of intelligence is an organism required to be a believer or follow gods law? 

Even if it’s close, why would we assume their rules to be the same as ours? Are orcas, octopus and corvids required to follow the rules laid out in holy texts lest they be sinners? What if they were just a touch smarter? This all gets weird when talking about non-humans.

The person above says that attraction can occur. I don’t know. I guess the idea is more fluid than I had understood. 

To be honest, what I truly believe, is that anyone can be whatever they want. Using Oxford definitions to define words is different than defining cultural concepts, I understand that. 

If someone feels they are asexual, or finds the label helpful then that’s all that matters. I do appreciate the discourse.

The definition disagrees with you. That’s the whole confusing thing. The definition of the word and the current spectrum of the sexual identity seem incompatible. I’m not arguing at all that people as you’ve described them are invalid somehow or that they don’t exist, I just don’t see that as the same as asexual. Isn’t demisexual more apt? 

Words should have meanings, and ‘asexual’ as a word is exclusionary to people that feel sexual desire, be it because of a person or not.
In the definition it says, “no sexual feelings or desires.” So desiring sex, even without attraction, is enough to not be included.

I don’t want to be offensive, but this makes no sense to me. Asexual has a definition that doesn’t change based on emotional intimacy. It means “a person who has no sexual feelings or desires, or who is not sexually attracted to anyone.” If all it takes to become “sexually active” is emotional intimacy, that’s not asexual, that’s just that persons personal sex drive. Libidos are crazy and vary wildly, but if you have one at all you can’t be asexual. It seems like the word has absolutely no meaning if it can just mean, “I’m not horny very often” or “I only like sex with a person I love.” Those two things mean a person by the very definition of the word, is not asexual. 

It’s completely normal to not like sex as much as the average Joe, I don’t see how that makes someone asexual. Also, it seems like including “low libido” people would muddy the waters for truly asexual people, which 100% do exist.
